applicability: Every integer. The rule holds because 100 ≡ 0 (mod 4), so N ≡ (N mod 100) (mod 4) for every integer N; single- and two-digit numbers are their own last two digits, and the sign is irrelevant.

steps.instruction: Only the last two digits matter

worked_example.result: not divisible by 4 (last two digits = 5, remainder 1)

operand_draw.notes: Range declared before draw. Filter constrains rendered width only (4-digit number), never divisibility. Drew a 4-digit number; the trick is answer-agnostic — this one happens to be not divisible by 4, which still demonstrates the mechanism instantly.

nulls.reason: The taught rule (a number is divisible by 4 iff its last two digits are) has no exception over the integers: 100 ≡ 0 (mod 4), so N mod 4 = (N mod 100) mod 4 for every integer N. Verified by exhaustive SymPy check over N ∈ [0, 100000] and by the modular identity itself.
